title: Shikhar Mohan: The 21-Year-Old Ranchi Opener Making Himself Count
excerpt: 613 Ranji runs at 55.73, twin fifties in the Duleep final, and a nod from Shahbaz Nadeem — Jharkhand's 21-year-old left-hander is forcing his way into the conversation.
body:
• Shikhar Mohan, a 21-year-old left-handed opener from Doranda, Ranchi, has emerged as Jharkhand's breakout batting talent — 613 runs at 55.73 in his debut Ranji season, the state's highest run-getter.
  • He started the 2026-27 season with 143 against Kerala at Jamshedpur, and starred in East Zone's Duleep Trophy final win at Chepauk with twin fifties (85 and 52) plus two wickets of left-arm spin.
  • Former India spinner Shahbaz Nadeem, now a Jharkhand cricket official, calls him "lambi race ka ghoda" — a long-term prospect with exceptional talent.
  • What this means for you: with India's top order in generational transition, domestic run-machines like Mohan are exactly who the selectors are watching — his name belongs on every diaspora fan's radar this Ranji season.

Ranchi has produced one generational cricketer in MS Dhoni and one white-ball star in Ishan Kishan. The city may be lining up a third. Shikhar Mohan, a 21-year-old left-handed opening batsman from Doranda who has lived in Ranchi all his life, has spent the last twelve months compiling the kind of domestic record that forces selectors to pay attention — and ESPNcricinfo's Duleep Trophy final report suggests the rest of the country is starting to notice.

The numbers

Mohan's debut first-class season in 2025-26: 613 runs in 12 innings at 55.73, including two centuries — Jharkhand's highest run-getter in the Ranji Trophy and in the 50-over Vijay Hazare Trophy. The arc within the season tells the story of a quick learner: out for 10 on debut against Tamil Nadu, then a double hundred against Nagaland, then 60 on a difficult pitch against Vidarbha, as Jharkhand reached the Ranji quarter-finals.

https://x.com/sportstarweb/status/2109202100479545578

He has started 2026-27 where he left off: 143 for Jharkhand against Kerala in the Ranji opener at Keenan Stadium, Jamshedpur. In the Duleep Trophy final at Chepauk in September, playing for East Zone at No. 3 — not his usual opening slot — he made twin fifties, 85 and 52, in East Zone's victory, and filled in for the injured Anukul Roy with 20 overs of left-arm spin, taking two wickets including N. Jagadeesan. Add an Irani Trophy 60 for Rest of India against defending champions Jammu & Kashmir on a green top in Srinagar, and T20 credentials — 322 runs at a strike rate near 170 in the 2026 Jharkhand Premier League — and the profile is that of a complete modern batter.

"Lambi race ka ghoda hai, alag hi talent hai." — He is a long-term prospect with exceptional talent.

— Shahbaz Nadeem, former India spinner and Jharkhand cricket official

The work behind it

Mohan's own assessment is notably unsentimental: "The second season is always more important because the opposition knows more about you… you have to keep improving." Before the Duleep Trophy he put himself through a rigorous 25-day training camp in Chennai, and he credits Ishan Kishan's guidance during the final — the Ranchi lineage, passed down in person. He has been photographed with Dhoni in Ranchi and with Kishan after the Duleep win: the city's cricketing royalty anointing its next prospect.

His stated goal is refreshingly collective: help Jharkhand win a red-ball tournament for the first time. RevSportz's profile captures the steadiness that teammates keep mentioning — the "sure, still and steadfast" temperament that separates prospects from products.

Why he matters now

Indian cricket's top order is in generational transition, and the selectors' gaze has swung decisively toward domestic weight of runs. A 21-year-old left-handed opener who scores in all three formats, bowls useful spin, and has already delivered in finals is precisely the profile that gets fast-tracked. The diaspora audience — which follows the Ranji Trophy's breakout names the way it once followed only internationals — should learn to spell Shikhar Mohan now. Ranchi's assembly line shows no signs of slowing.
